description: Set up to 200 cells of a table you run. Usually a cell gives `value` and `origin` (`entered`, `imported` with a `note` like the file or email it came from, `link` with its `source`, or `generated`). Left out, the origin is `link` when there's a `source` and `generated` when there isn't. These can go into a published table too, and never replace a quoted value. A date is written YYYY-MM-DD, and a column with choices takes only one of them. In a table that requires proof, a cell instead gives `value`, `source` and `quote`, word for word from the source; each page is opened before it's saved, so send at most 25 of these at once, and only into a draft. If no acceptable source states it, give `checked` with the pages you read, and `none_stated` only if you read the whole source and it has no such value. The reply counts what saved and lists only the cells that didn't, with a reason, and `unchecked` names quoted values whose page couldn't be read. Needs a token.

note.description: How a value without a quote was made, such as the prompt that generated it

origin.description: Where a value without a quote came from. Only in a table whose proof is optional

name: fill_cells
